name: Budapest
title: Budapest in December
lead: Three days on foot on both sides of the Danube. Viewpoints by day, markets and thermal baths after dark, because the sun sets before 16:00.
facts: Sunrise around 7:20, sunset around 15:55. The best light is around 15:00. All times are Budapest time, one hour behind Bulgarian time.
Usually between −2 and 4 °C, often grey and windy by the river. Bring warm shoes with a non-slip sole.

Vörösmarty Square and the Basilica markets usually run from mid or late November until 31 December or 1 January, roughly 11:00 or 12:00 until 21:00–22:00. Exact dates for this year were not confirmed when this was written; check before you go.
On 24, 25 and 26 December many restaurants, the markets and the baths have shorter hours or close. The Central Market Hall is closed on Sundays and on 25–26 December.
Hungarian forint (HUF). Cards are accepted almost everywhere; some market stalls prefer cash.
Bring your own swimsuit, flip-flops and towel to save on rentals. Tickets are cheaper online.
note: The maps are approximate, not to scale, and routes are straight lines between stops. For the real street route use the “Open route” button. Opening hours, prices and dates come from public sources and may change. The “Photos” links open an image search.

days.title: Parliament, Basilica and the Pest markets
days.theme: Start at the Parliament, see the city from the Basilica dome, watch the sunset by the Danube and spend the evening at the two big Christmas markets.

stops.name: Parliament and Kossuth Square
stops.d: Walk around the building from outside before the tour groups arrive. Guided tours inside are paid and sell out; book online if you want one.

stops.name: Shoes on the Danube Bank
stops.d: A memorial to the Jews shot into the river in 1944–45, on the embankment south of the Parliament.
stops.q: Shoes on the Danube Bank Budapest

stops.name: Coffee or breakfast near the Parliament
stops.d: Three places within a few minutes' walk.

opts.s: cakes and breakfast, chocolate museum upstairs
family pastry shop, almost 100 years old
specialty coffee

stops.name: St Stephen's Basilica and the dome
stops.d: Climb (or take the lift) to the panorama terrace around the dome for a 360° view over Pest and the castle. Paid entry.

stops.name: Lunch with Hungarian food
stops.d: Goulash, paprikás and lángos. Book ahead in December or come before 12:30.

opts.s: Hungarian bistro next to the Hold Street market hall
home-style Hungarian cooking near the Parliament
classic bistro, two minutes from the Basilica

stops.name: Danube Promenade
stops.d: Walk south along the Pest bank from the Chain Bridge to the Vigadó, with the Castle and Gellért Hill across the river.

stops.name: Sunset over Buda
stops.d: The sun sets around 15:55. Watch the Castle and the Chain Bridge light up from the Pest end of the bridge.

stops.name: Christmas market on Vörösmarty Square
stops.d: The oldest Christmas market in the city: crafts, chimney cake (kürtőskalács), sausages, stuffed cabbage and mulled wine (forralt bor).

stops.name: Advent market at the Basilica
stops.d: Light show projected on the Basilica façade in the evening, an ice rink around the tree, and food stalls.

stops.name: Dinner
stops.d: All three are within ten minutes of the Basilica. Book ahead.

opts.s: modern Hungarian food and a long Hungarian wine list
Hungarian dishes from family recipes
pork and Hungarian classics near the Opera

days.title: Castle Hill, Gellért Hill and a thermal bath
days.theme: Cross the Chain Bridge, spend the morning on Castle Hill, catch the sunset from Gellért Hill and warm up in a Turkish bath.

stops.name: Across the Chain Bridge
stops.d: Walk over the bridge to Clark Ádám Square. Take the funicular (paid) or the free steps and paths up to the palace.

stops.name: Buda Castle courtyards
stops.d: Walk through the palace courtyards and onto the terrace above the Danube. The National Gallery is inside if you want a museum.

stops.name: Coffee and pastry on Castle Hill
stops.d: Two classic pastry shops and a hotel café, all in the old town on the hill.

opts.s: pastry shop open since the 1820s; very small, expect a queue
strudel (rétes) with cherry, poppy seed or cottage cheese
café and bar in a boutique hotel at the north end of the hill

stops.name: Fisherman's Bastion and Matthias Church
stops.d: The view over the Parliament is free from the lower terraces; the upper towers and the church are paid.

stops.name: Lunch on Castle Hill
stops.d: All three are within a few minutes of Matthias Church.

opts.s: modern takes on Hungarian classics
café-restaurant in an old bakery; check days, it has not always opened every day
Hungarian food in a medieval building
opts.q: Fortuna Restaurant Budapest Hess András tér

stops.name: Down through the Tabán
stops.d: Leave the hill by the southern paths and cross the Tabán park towards the Elisabeth Bridge and the foot of Gellért Hill.

stops.name: Sunset from Gellért Hill and the Citadella
stops.d: The climb takes about 30 minutes. The terraces and the Liberty Statue are free; the exhibition in the Citadella, which reopened in 2026, is paid. Sunset is around 15:55.

stops.name: Rudas Baths
stops.d: A 16th-century Turkish bath at the foot of the hill, with a rooftop pool looking over the Danube. Bring a swimsuit and flip-flops. Check holiday hours around 24–26 December.

stops.name: Dinner
stops.d: One on the Buda side, two across the Liberty Bridge in Pest.

opts.s: game and Hungarian dishes in the Tabán, 10 minutes from Rudas
cellar restaurant behind the National Museum
Spanish tapas and wine

days.title: Market Hall, Jewish Quarter and City Park
days.theme: Shop for paprika at the Central Market Hall, walk the Jewish Quarter and Andrássy Avenue, and end the day in the Széchenyi Baths.

stops.name: Central Market Hall
stops.d: Paprika, salami, Tokaji wine and lángos upstairs. Closed on Sundays and on 25–26 December; open until 15:00 on Saturdays.

stops.name: Breakfast or coffee
stops.d: One in the hall and two on the way north.

opts.n: Lángos stalls, upper floor of the Central Market Hall
opts.s: fried dough with sour cream and cheese
specialty coffee in a courtyard

opts.n: My Little Melbourne, Madách Imre út 3
opts.s: coffee and breakfast near Deák Square

stops.name: Dohány Street Synagogue
stops.d: The largest synagogue in Europe. Paid entry; closed on Saturdays and Jewish holidays.

stops.name: Jewish Quarter: Kazinczy utca and Gozsdu udvar
stops.d: Ruin bars, street art and the Kazinczy Street Synagogue. Szimpla Kert, the first ruin bar, is open by day.

stops.name: Lunch in the Jewish Quarter
stops.d: Three different styles in the same few streets.

opts.s: goulash and paprikás in a small dining room
Israeli and Middle Eastern food under a glass roof
street-food court next to Szimpla Kert

stops.name: Andrássy Avenue and the Opera
stops.d: Walk up the avenue past the Opera House. If your legs are tired, take the yellow M1 metro under it to Hősök tere.

stops.name: Heroes' Square at sunset
stops.d: The Millennium Monument and the two museums in the last light.

stops.name: Vajdahunyad Castle and the City Park ice rink
stops.d: The lake becomes one of Europe's largest open-air ice rinks in winter (paid, skates for hire).

stops.name: Széchenyi Baths
stops.d: The big yellow bath with outdoor pools that steam in the cold. Bring a swimsuit and flip-flops. Check holiday hours around 24–26 December.

stops.name: Dinner
stops.d: Two in City Park, one back near the Opera.

opts.s: the city's most famous classic restaurant; formal and pricey
on a small island in the City Park lake
retro-styled Hungarian food on a lively square
